_meta.indication: Indicated for use in positron emission tomography (PET) to visualize dopaminergic nerve terminals in the striatum for the evaluation of adult patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndromes (PS); PET is an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated; conducted under Expanded Access IND 78861
pivotal_trials.phase: Prospective single-center imaging study (adequate and well-controlled)
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, single-center study in which binary interpretations of 18F-FDOPA scans by 3 independent blinded readers were analyzed for agreement with a clinical reference standard of PS or non-PS, established by a minimum of 6 months of patient follow-up by a blinded movement disorder specialist.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients (18 years or older) with at least one cardinal symptom of PS (bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor, postural instability) referred for further evaluation due to diagnostic uncertainty; of 56 completers, 38 (68%) male, 18 (32%) female, mean age 66 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints were positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between binary 18F-FDOPA PET results and the binary clinical reference standard diagnosis (PS or non-PS) at follow-up.
pivotal_trials.n: 56 patients completed at least 6-month follow-up and were included in the efficacy analysis (68 underwent 18F-FDOPA of 69 recruited)
pivotal_trials.result: Across the 3 readers (n=56), NPA ranged 83–91% and PPA ranged 49–73%: Reader 1 PPA 73 (95% CI 55, 87), NPA 91 (72, 99); Reader 2 PPA 49 (31, 67), NPA 91 (72, 99); Reader 3 PPA 58 (39, 75), NPA 83 (61, 94).

key_safety: No adverse reactions reported in the open-label trial of 68 patients (plus 53 additional exposures). In Study #18, all 12 observed adverse events (e.g., headache n=2, tiredness n=3) were mild, non-serious, resolved without intervention, and assessed as unlikely related; no deaths or serious AEs. Injection site pain identified in foreign postmarketing experience.
target_moa: 18F-FDOPA is a radiolabeled analog of levodopa that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted to F-18 fluorodopamine by aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD) in the striatum, where it is stored in vesicles of dopaminergic neuron terminals; in PS, striatal uptake/storage is reduced, so it acts as a marker of dopaminergic neurodegeneration on PET.
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (PET radiodiagnostic; F-18 radiolabeled analog of levodopa)

rems.type: No REMS; the review's REMS section states None.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was conducted; the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

summary.text: 18F-FDOPA was approved as a 505(b)(2) NDA (NDA 200655) reviewed as a Class 2 Resubmission responding to a prior Complete Response letter; approval was based on prospective Study #18. No REMS and no postmarketing requirements or commitments were required, and the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

basis.text: The prior submission's clinical data (a retrospective chart review of 185 patients) were found inadequate to support the proposed indication; FDA recommended a prospective clinical study.

citations.quote: The submitted clinical data was based on a retrospective chart review of 185 patients at the Applicant's institution. FDA review found the submitted clinical data to be inadequate to support the proposed indication and issued a Complete Response (CR) letter dated 10/22/2013. The FDA recommended that the Applicant conduct a prospective clinical study to support the proposed indication.
